title: Dancing dots: The motion-sickness cure hidden in iPhone settings
excerpt: A buried iPhone setting is turning heads and saving stomachs. But does relief just mean more time staring at your screen?
content_html:
1 day ago

Thomas Germain

A buried iPhone setting is turning heads and saving stomachs. But does relief just mean more time staring at your screen?

I try not to look at other people's phones, but you get unintentional glances jammed in the crowds on the New York subway, bodies lurching around as the train blasts through tunnels. Lately I've noticed something strange. I keep seeing people with dots dancing across their screens.

The more I saw it, the more I needed to know. It turns out all these people have something in common: they get motion sickness.

This choreographed dot ballet is a lesser-known iPhone setting called "Vehicle Motion Cues" that's supposed to help. It puts animated dots on the edges of your screen, which move in sync with the motion of the vehicle you're in, thanks to the phone's accelerometer.

Reviews are mixed, but over the past few months, some people have gone wild for it. One man I met on the subway told me he loves the feature so much he keeps it on 24 hours a day, even when he's not moving – though he declined to share his name with the strange journalist asking questions on his commute.

The dots could be an antidote if you're cursed with a history of queasy car rides. I was born with an iron stomach, so I'm afraid I can't relate. But I think there's something more interesting happening. Bit by bit, our devices are adapting to infiltrate more of our lives.

A phone for what ails you

Here's some trivia I learned talking to doctors for this story: it seems like most of the people who study motion sickness get motion sickness.

"When I go on a cruise, I'm in my bunk for like 72 to 96 hours. I can't eat, I can't get up," says Tom Stoffregen, professor emeritus at the University of Minnesota, US, who's been studying motion sickness since the 1980s.

Experts disagree about what causes motion sickness. The classic explanation is "sensory conflict theory": your inner ear detects movement, but other senses (like your sight) see a bunch of fixed objects that seem like they aren't going anywhere.

Stoffregen doesn't buy it. Instead, he says the issue is your muscles and other bodily systems are constantly guessing where you're about to move to control your posture, and you get discombobulated when the prediction fails. That might explain why passengers get sick but drivers usually don't, because they're controlling the car.

Either way, the confusion makes some of us nauseous, says Kristen Steenerson, a clinical associate professor at Stanford University, US, who studies the vestibular system, which controls balance.

"That deviation is what makes people feel dizzy, or disoriented," says Steenerson. "And probably due to some interesting evolutionary coincidences, that elicits a lot of nausea." We may have evolved to assume we've eaten something toxic when we feel disoriented, she says, so your body thinks it a good time to vomit.

If you can give your body signals that demonstrate how you're moving through space, it can mitigate motion sickness, Steenerson says. The iPhone's dots seem to follow the same logic. "They give you a sense of how you are moving in space," she says.

"There is some research that has looked into visual feedback and found it can be very helpful," says Steenerson. For example, you can buy phenomenally goofy anti-nausea glasses that are filled with liquid that sloshes around in a similar fashion, and there's evidence they work. If you've never seen them, I am delighted to present you with the photo below.

Steenerson says the dots help a little with her own motion sickness. "Everyone thinks there's something wrong with my screen. These dots are so cool," she says.

To turn it on, open your iPhone Settings > Accessibility > Motion > Vehicle Motion Cues. You can leave the dots on perpetually or have them turn on automatically when your phone detects motion. Android apps can replicate the setting, and there are rumours a similar feature is coming to Pixel phones.

You can also change the size and colour. I've been walking around with big purple dots on my screen that make for great conversation starters.

Some motion sickness victims told me vehicle motion cues didn't help, but some people call them a miracle.

Zandie Brockett, a curator from New York City, swears by them. "It's been a game changer," she says, enough to turn her into an iPhone-dots evangelist. "I'm not screaming about them from the rooftops. But I recommend them anytime someone tells me they get car sick."

I heard the same from my old boss, Rory Carroll. His car sickness is particularly ironic, as he spends a lot of time in the passenger's seat for work: he's editor-in-chief of Alloy, a car enthusiast news publication. "It's a bit of an occupational hazard," Caroll says. "It's solving a very specific problem that I've had my whole life. The dots really work."

Fans of the iPhone dots kept telling me the same observation. They are only useful when you get motion sick because you're looking at your phone.

In other words, your reward is yet another opportunity to look at your screen. Which isn't a reward at all, perhaps, when so many people worry about screen time. "It is a bit of a bummer to have one less reason not to look at Instagram," says Carroll.

More like this:

Phones consume modern life, and new developments are letting them creep into the few remaining times we can't use them. Ever-growing battery life means screens stay on for longer. Elon Musk and his competitors have blanketed the sky with satellites that beam Wi-Fi and phone service to once disconnected areas.

There's even a rumour that Apple is working AirPods with cameras in them, not for taking photos, but to serve as eyes for new AI voice tools you can use screen-free. It may allow for new computing opportunities in those rare phoneless moments, like when you're walking down the street.

If looking at screens makes you car sick, you might want to try the iPhone dots. Or – stop me if this sounds crazy – you could just put your phone down and enjoy the ride.

content_html_zh:
1 天前

托马斯·杰曼

埋藏在地下的 iPhone 设置不仅能吸引眼球，还能节省肚子。 但缓解仅仅意味着有更多时间盯着屏幕吗？

我尽量不看别人的手机，但在纽约地铁的人群中，你会无意中看到别人的目光，当火车冲过隧道时，人们的身体摇摇晃晃。 最近我注意到一些奇怪的事情。 我经常看到带有圆点的人在屏幕上跳舞。

我看到的越多，我就越需要了解。 事实证明，所有这些人都有一个共同点：他们都会晕车。

这个精心设计的点芭蕾舞是一个不太为人所知的 iPhone 设置，称为“车辆运动提示”，应该会有所帮助。 它会在屏幕边缘放置动画点，借助手机的加速计，这些动画点会与您所在车辆的运动同步移动。

评论褒贬不一，但在过去的几个月里，有些人为之疯狂。 我在地铁上遇到的一位男士告诉我，他非常喜欢这个功能，所以每天 24 小时都开着这个功能，即使他不动的时候也是如此——尽管他拒绝透露自己的名字，但他拒绝向在通勤时提问的陌生记者透露自己的名字。

如果你有坐车不舒服的经历，这些点可能是一剂解药。 我天生铁胃，恐怕无法体会。 但我认为还有更有趣的事情发生。 我们的设备正在一点一点地适应并渗透到我们的生活中。

一部解决您烦恼的手机

以下是我在与医生交谈时了解到的一些琐事：似乎大多数研究晕动病的人都患有晕动病。

“当我乘坐游轮时，我会在铺位上待 72 到 96 个小时。 我吃不下，起不来，”美国明尼苏达大学名誉教授汤姆·斯托弗雷根 (Tom Stoffregen) 说道，他自 20 世纪 80 年代以来一直在研究晕动病。

专家们对于晕车的原因存在不同意见。 经典的解释是“感觉冲突理论”：你的内耳检测到运动，但其他感官（例如你的视觉）看到一堆固定的物体，它们似乎不会去任何地方。

斯托弗雷根并不买账。 相反，他说问题在于你的肌肉和其他身体系统不断猜测你将要移动到哪里来控制你的姿势，当预测失败时你会感到混乱。 这也许可以解释为什么乘客会生病，但司机通常不会生病，因为他们控制着汽车。

无论哪种方式，这种混乱都会让我们中的一些人感到恶心，美国斯坦福大学临床副教授克里斯汀·斯蒂恩森（Kristen Steenerson）说，他研究控制平衡的前庭系统。

“这种偏差让人感到头晕或迷失方向，”斯蒂森说。 “可能是由于一些有趣的进化巧合，这引起了很多恶心。” 她说，当我们感到迷失方向时，我们可能已经进化到认为我们吃了有毒的东西，所以你的身体认为这是呕吐的好时机。

斯蒂恩森说，如果你可以向身体发出信号来表明你如何在太空中移动，就可以减轻晕动病。 iPhone 的圆点似乎也遵循同样的逻辑。 “它们让你了解自己如何在太空中移动，”她说。

“有一些研究研究了视觉反馈，发现它非常有帮助，”斯廷森说。 例如，你可以购买非常愚蠢的防恶心眼镜，里面装满液体，以类似的方式晃动，并且有证据表明它们有效。 如果您从未见过它们，我很高兴向您展示下面的照片。

斯蒂恩森说，这些点对她自己的晕车症有一点帮助。 “每个人都认为我的屏幕有问题。 这些点太酷了，”她说。

要打开它，请打开 iPhone 设置 > 辅助功能 > 运动 > 车辆运动提示。 您可以让这些点永久打开，也可以在手机检测到运动时自动打开它们。 Android 应用程序可以复制该设置，有传言称 Pixel 手机也将推出类似功能。

您还可以更改尺寸和颜色。 我一直在屏幕上带着紫色的大圆点走来走去，这些大圆点是很好的对话开场白。

一些晕车患者告诉我，车辆运动提示没有帮助，但有些人称其为奇迹。

来自纽约市的策展人赞迪·布罗克特 (Zandie Brockett) 对它们深信不疑。 “这改变了游戏规则，”她说，足以让她成为 iPhone dots 的传播者。 “我不会在屋顶上为他们尖叫。 但只要有人告诉我他们晕车了，我就会推荐他们。”

我从我的前任老板罗里·卡罗尔那里听到了同样的说法。 他的晕车现象尤其具有讽刺意味，因为他工作的大部分时间都在副驾驶座上：他是汽车爱好者新闻刊物 Alloy 的主编。 “这有点职业危害，”卡罗尔说。 “它正在解决我一生都面临的一个非常具体的问题。 这些点确实有效。”

iPhone 圆点的粉丝们不断地告诉我同样的观察结果。 它们仅在您因为看手机而晕车时才有用。

换句话说，您的奖励是另一个查看屏幕的机会。 当这么多人担心屏幕时间时，这也许根本不是一种奖励。 卡罗尔表示：“少了一个不看 Instagram 的理由，这有点令人遗憾。”

更多类似这样的：

手机消耗着现代生活，而新的发展让它们悄悄进入了我们仅剩的少数无法使用手机的时代。 不断增长的电池寿命意味着屏幕的开启时间更长。 埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和他的竞争对手已经用卫星覆盖了整个天空，将 Wi-Fi 和电话服务传输到曾经断开连接的区域。

甚至有传言称，苹果正在为 AirPods 配备摄像头，不是为了拍照，而是为了充当新的人工智能语音工具的眼睛，让你可以在没有屏幕的情况下使用。 它可能会在那些罕见的无电话时刻（例如当您走在街上时）提供新的计算机会。

如果看屏幕会让你晕车，你可能想尝试一下 iPhone 的圆点。 或者——如果这听起来很疯狂，请阻止我——你可以放下手机，享受这段旅程。
